sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.
Recognise details in shapes and objects as being similar or different from each other.
Tell a story using pictures.
Follow lines with a finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare illustrations
• Show pupils how to open their Pupil Books to the 
first page. Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils 
can see the page for Lesson 1 and point to the first 
illustration.
• Say: Jinen musinkam mooluul di fáteemenaaf fati di buwuloorumab buto ŋandab nan mo'ome. 
Uye énukuruŋ yéy ma?
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of the bull. 
• Say: "Jinenaal musinkam moololaal di buwuloorumab butooŋandab. Mante sinannaam di 
• bábilewuumi? A'aa! 
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: "Jijikeraal bábilewuumi.  Mante sinannaam di butooŋandab?  A'aa!'
• Point to the final picture in the row. 
• Say: Mante ube bunannaam di butooŋandab ?  Éey
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches.
Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the Pupil Book.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Jinen musinkam mooluul di buwuloorumab butoŋandab . Anaw waawu nambo ekaan?" 
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what the 
people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. Help them see 
that the woman is preparing "banku".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Áriiŋaaw ammi di buwuloorumab ube waawu nambo ekaan?  Jirambenaalool man anag 
maalaay enoken bee di bulaamab!  Jijonjoojonjoor?  Jiŋar jisinkaj jooluul jíridaj man jíyisen 
buruŋab bee di maalaay.
• Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger.
• Say: "Eñeraay waawu yoomu bo di ekaan?  Waawu nusofe mati woo emaŋumi?"
• Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger.
• Repeat with the remaining image.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Recognize the front cover, back cover, and title of a book.
Apply new words learned to own life and use new words in conversation.
Use background knowledge to build meaning.
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, 
back, title
• Point to the cover and back of a book.
• Say: Wulaal eliikum ñetum fáculey bee di 
bálamukab.  Ute too emmi katojak kúfaculaak kati 
búkaay.  
• Say: Kurimak  kammi di kúfaculey yati katojak koo kuregeyiimi fujuumaf fati búkaay.  Fujuumaf 
footumi káyisenak wan ootaami eliikey.
• Say: Nampi úriiŋaami tan karegak kuremi, pan ujukaal bálamukab bati búkaay." 
• This is the front page of the book.
• Point to the cover and back of a book.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils what 
they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
• If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
ajeloorool  atekelak

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such as 
when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned.
Faatu Natiititiiti
Faatu súumutool. Oomu man alakoe síndeey balet di waaf. Najukumi asom oola Binta di etampey 
yati bálutab.
"Asom, mante erambeni?"
"Hée a'aa,  Faatu, wan uliikemi ujuupojuupo máamak!"
Ñaa nápurumi ajaw awuuj.
Najukumi mati ajeloorool oomu bo najoonen katekelak koola jooŋoor.
"Atiom, mante  erambeni?" 
"Hée a'aa, Faatu, wan uliikemi ujuupojuupo máamak!"
Ñaa nápurumi ajaw awuuj.
Ñaa najukumi áliinool oomu bo káruugenak di kafatak.
"Áliinom, mante erambeni?"
"Hée a'aa, Faatu, wan uliikemi ujuupojuupo máamak!"
Ñaa nápurumi ajwa awuuj.
burokab bati di fuliitikenaf. "Atiyom, mante  erambeni?" "Hée a'aa, Faatu, wan uliikemi 
ujuupojuupo máamak!"
Nan púrutomi, najwumi baari ampaol.  Ampaol naceeŋoomi,
'Añiilaw úmboom Faatu, waa nubolene ñaa?'
"Wan iliikemi ujuupojuupo máamak itampujaat bálutab. Wan iliikemi ujuupojuupo máamak 
ijoonenujaat utekelaw.  Wan iliikemi ujuupojuupo máamak íruugenujaat di kafatak. Ban poop 
niliikeliik juupo máamak kaanujaat burokab bati di fuliitikenaf. Waawu neete ekaan?"
 Ampaol naanoomi,
"Hée Faatu!  Takumbi ubolen! Kabaakak kooli kureewooreewoor.  Ínje nimammaŋ an uñenaw       
woola uliikenumi man arambenom ijoonen sileemunaas di muceesam.  Mante pan urambenom?"
Ñaa narambenoomi.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading from. Ask 
what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")
• Say: Tótey nujukumi fujuumaf fati karegak?    
• (correct response: ("Fáculey yati káfimenumaak kati búkaay")
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer. Call on a second volunteer pupil to say the title of the 
story that was just read aloud.
• Say: Nampi úriiŋaami di fúbanumaf fati búkaay waawu nootaale bee ejuk? 
• (correct response: "Bálamukab bati káfimenumaak kati búkaay")
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.Language-Less

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes, and wi.th a finger.
Recognize details in letter shapes as being similar or different from each other
Follow lines with their finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters  
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the 
page and point to the first capital letter. Do not say 
the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for 
pupils to learn letters. It is an activity for pupils to 
practice telling the difference between letter and 
shapes. 
• Say : Ínje bee eŋar  jisinkaj júboom man iñuur eciikaay etooŋandey.  Hani an di muyuul 
takumbi aŋar jisinkaj joola man añuur.  Wulaal pambi ujikeraal waaf uceen wanammi net di 
uwe."
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Jinenaal kusinkak koololaal di eciikaay etooŋandey.  Mante sinannaam di etooŋandey?  
A'aa!'
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Jijikeraal yabilewuumi.  Mante sinannaam di etooŋandey?  
• Point to the final one in the row.
• Say: Mante sinannaam di etooŋandey? Éey! 
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it.
Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page of the Pupil 
Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It is 
an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. Ask pupils to 
point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct answer).

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Say: Jiriibenaal múyitaam ume! Mutooŋandam esiinooraay!  Jinenaal musinkam moololaal di 
fútooŋumaf man uriibenaal man epopemi di eeno di katojak. 
• Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
• Repeat with the remaining images.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Know that words are separated by spaces.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Answer factual questions.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Words are separated by spaces
activities.content:
Describe what a word is, and why there are 
spaces between them
• Take out the read aloud book from yesterday's 
lesson.
• Choose a sentence to write on the board. 
• In a sentence. When I read, I read each word one by one, because every word has a meaning.
• Say: Kasankenak uke di karegak kan ireguumi kúpurumulo.
      Pan usankenaal mati baŋaanab bammi di kurimak di kasenkenak.  Nampi ilakomi eliikey, ínje   
      eliik furim fákon fákon, mati furim fanoofani fubabaj wan fufele.
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: Baŋaanab bammi titoorey yati kurimak búyisenyisen bóbey furimaf fujuumenimi di bóbey 
furimaf futooŋumi."
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Say: Baŋaanab bati kurimak burambeneyiramben  mambi iŋoolen uliik.  Nampi uciikumi 
kasankenak kanaamutak, pan ukaten baŋaanab di titoorey yati kurimak.
• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new sentence.
• Say: Jinen kusinkak kooluul di fáteemenaaf fati furimaf.  
• Ñaa jiyisof furimaf fabielwuuumi.  
• Buu noote káyisen eeno mati kurimak uke kugabaarak kunaamut.
• correct response: (baŋaanab boobu to titooraay yooli ko.)
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two words, and 
put their fingers on it.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.
Recognize sight words.
Read sentences using sight words and pictures.
Draw simple shapes.

activities.title: Read sight words
activities.content:
Learn two new sight words
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in the Pupil 
Book.
• Say: Ume BUUBA.  Ume KADI.  Pambi uliikaal waaf 
wajuupoe wooliil di  bucaabab ube.
• fútemenaaf fati furimaf KADI  Di fútemenaaf fati 
buwuloorumab bati jímajiraay.
• Say: Jinen musinkam mooluul di fútemenaaf fati furimaf Buba.  Di fúteemenaaf fati 
buwuloorumab bati áriiŋaaw.  Jinen musinkam mooluul di
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to [BOY NAME] Buba on the left side, then point to the matching name on the 
right side. Repeat with [GIRL NAME]. Kaddy
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching name in the row.
• Continue in the same way with each row.

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say: Ínje nijujuk KADI di fatiyaay yati katojak uke.  Iñeme nijujuk furim funkul!  Furimaf ufe 
funkulaf foone (jiker).  Numanjaamanj KADI di furimaf ufe funkulaf, pan uŋoolenaal uliikaal 
wan uwuloorumaw uwe úyisenumi.
• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to name the 
picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the pictures/word 
with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.
• Point to pictures or words as you read. [BOY NAME sees a goat].  Buuba najujuk ejaameney
• Remind pupils that káninguloor" mba "ejuk means "to observe" or "to see."
• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture sentence again 
together.
• Say: Iñeme ay jijuke tentaamey?  Jinenaal musinkam moololaal di kasankenak ban nuliikaal 
• kasankenak poopolaal (Kadi najujuk taabuley).

• Say: Ay pan aŋoolen aliik kasankenak kariibenumi?
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects 
• Point to the next activity in the Pupil Book.
• Say: "Jinenaal musinkam moololaal di buwuloorumab  butooŋandab.  Waawu jijuke?  Mante 
jijuk ejunkutey yaatumi ebiley?"
• Point to the next picture in the row.
• Say: Éey, ébeey!  Waawu wanaamutumi titoorey yati ébeey di esahaay?
• Continue with other illustrations.

activities.title: Draw shapes
activities.content:
Practice drawing common shapes
• Ask pupils to trace each shape in the Pupil Book with one finger.
• Ask pupils to try to draw 3 of each shape in their exercise books. Depending on their comfort 
with writing and drawing, different pupils may focus on just one shape or draw many.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger
• Say: "Nampi ilakomi eliikey, ínje kajiker furim fákon, 
fákon.  Furim fanoofani fubabaj wan fufele.  Man 
úlawul wan ommi di eliikey, babaj fúkaw máamak 
man uliik furim fanoofani." Eneney yati  jisinkaj  
jooli di fáteemenaaf fati furim fanoosani pan 
rambeni takumbi úyuur hani furim."
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate how to track with your finger under each word as 
you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger under the specific word.
• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while you read it 
aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils what they 
know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If needed, 
help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
kásumutak, kasontenak, kujuudoorumi.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or  supplementary illustrations if available
• Partway through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your finger below 
each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make a big sweeping motion 
back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking with your finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud.
Aadama ayinkunaaw nababaj kásumutak kati Foocaay
Aadama ayinkunaaw oo di inaa oola di baa oola kucine.
Inaa oola di baa oola di kuwonkool, "Aadama!" kalimbisak di kutunten sii.  Kujamut hani kayel kati 
an.  Aadama óomey?
Aadama najam inaa oola nawonkool.  Najam baa oola nawonkool.  Aadama ayiigut.  Narunlen 
kafintaak di bacaacab.
oola di baa oola di kujuudoorumi.  Inaa oola nateyumi bee di kalimbisak kati Aadama.
Inaa oola naan, "Aadama saafi.  Buu nukaane?"  Aadama nalaaŋenool,, "Háa inaa. Íjne íjuut!"  
Inaa oola nanennumi  kañenak koola di fúriiŋaf fati Aadama ban naanool, "Aw eniiley éboliboli! 
Pan íwonkul  asontenaaw !" Baa oola najaw ewonkey yati asontenaaw ñetum di mobaaley.
Asontenaaw nabil alaapen Aadama ban naan, aw  "Eniiley éboliboli!  Ñaa pan usontenaal 
kásumutak kooli!
Aadama faraf foola di furi, "naceeŋ, Asontenaaw, asontenaaw! Mante ínje bee ecet room?"
Alaakaw náluumi aban naan, "A'aa, Aadama! Ínje bee eseni bubeebenab ban pan úmoori!"
Inaa oola nammi, "Asontenaaw, Emit ekati!"  "Asontenaaw nammi, takumbi újim mati 
bubeebenab.  Kápurumul jaat bee fácul, Aadama nawaarene afinto di sankaay yan kukammi 
bubeebenab bati bawolab.
Inaa najikerumi baa ban nammi, "Noomaal sankaay yati bawolab jaat! Bonket! Utey galab bee di 
funoomenaf!"  Aadama najamiil di kusanken ban nalaañumi afinto. 
Ure kankaan kareg kati kuñiilak bee mati  kapakenak di kasontenak kati kásumutak kati bawola, 
di káliŋen wabajumi fúkaw bee di fusontenaf di eŋarey yati sankaay yati bawolab yan kujooneumi 
bubeebenab.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their own 
words.
• Say: Ñaa uŋarulaal kurima kan uliikenlaami man ujoonenaal ko kasanken.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a 
new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't skip words while 
reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or follow under the words with 
your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Ask pupils to try to read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned previously. 
Monitor and help pupils as needed.
• After giving pupils an opportunity to read the sentences independently, call on a pupil at 
random to read the first sentence. Ask another pupil to read the second, then continue for 
each of the sentences. Ensure that pupils know the correct way to read each sentence.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who" ("ayima")
Read the question: 
• Say: Awonkumi asontenaaw ay nan Aadama ájuutumi? 
• Answer: (Aadama baa oola awonkumi asontenaaw nan Aadama ájuutumi)
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "ay" is asking about. Call on one or two 
pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word  "ay" asks us the name of a someone or something alive)
• Teach pupils to use the question word  ("bóbey")
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, ("bóbey") Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: 
• Say: Nampi úsumutumi bóbey nujawemi?
• Say: Furimaf "bóbey" foo fúyisenewolaami mante ban mba mukaanaay.  Nampi jijammi bóbey di 
jimanj mati kúlaaŋenak pan kukaan bucin.
• Read the question: 
• Say: "Aadama bóbey  nalakoe nan Inaa oola di Baa oola kulakomi ewonkooley?"  Kúlaa ŋenak: 
"Aadama di kalimbisak koola nalakoe nan Inaa oola di Baa oola kulakomi ewonkooley.
• Say: Ujonlenaal síwoonooras soololaal bee tan uliikulaami.  Kámikak wan kúyisenumi woo emmi 
oomuto man  afintoe di bacaacab bee iñeme.
• Ask pupils to think about "where", or the place, that this happened.
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: 
• Aadama Baa oola bóbey nanoomulo sankaay?
• Answer:  (Aadama Baa oola di funoomenaf nanoomulo sankaay).
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. Remind pupils that it is a  "bóbey" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Evaluate pupils use of the keyword "where" ("Bóbey") 
• Say: Question Introduction: What word can we identify that asks about a place or situation in 
a story?
• Call on a pupil at random who raised their hand. Remind them that the word is "where" 
(bóbey)

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book, spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
1. Know what the "cover " and "back " of the 
book means.
2. Understand that words in print are separated by 
spaces.
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps 
keep track of where you are reading.
1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means.
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and explain. Give more 
examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure to support them in this skill during 
the next lessons.
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "back" of the book. Give feedback, and explain 
and give more examples if needed.
2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture for the story, 
so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read this story yet, but that is 
alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put their finger on 
that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: Baŋaanab bammi titoorey yooli ko boo  búyisenumi mati uku kurim kugaba kanaamut.
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are reading
• Open a big book (any big book) to the first page. Ask pupils to watch and listen. Read the first 
sentence while pointing to (tracking) each word with your finger.
• Ask pupils what you were doing with your finger. Then ask them why you did that. Tell the pupil 
who responds if they are correct or not. Then repeat or say the correct response. (Possible 
response: I was tracking a finger under the words as I read them. Tracking with a finger helps 
you know where you are while reading, so you don't get confused or lost.)

activities.title: Reinforcement Activity
activities.content:
NOTE
• Look at the list of key skills below. Choose one that your pupils need to practice. Ask pupils to 
turn back to that page in the Pupil Book and repeat that activity.
Key activities from week 1 lessons
1. Draw lines and shapes
2. Read sentences with sight words
3. Choose the letter that matches the first letter in the row
4. Recognize sight words (character names)

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Tell a story using pictures.
Recognize sight words, and read them in a sentence.
Track words from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Point to the picture story in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Place your finger under the first picture. What 
is the person doing?
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence 
(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what the people are 
doing in each picture and ask questions to help 
them think about the pictures.
• Say: Jinen musinkam mooluul di fátemenaaf fati buwuloorumab butooŋandab.  Anaw waawu nambo 
ekaan?
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling.

activities.title: Read a sentence using sight words
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to independently read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned 
yesterday. Walk around the room to monitor and help pupils as needed. Ensure that pupils are 
reading from left to right and tracking the pictures/words with their finger.
• After giving pupils an opportunity to read the sentences, call on pupils at random to read aloud 
the first 6 picture sentences.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Identify and say the target vowel sound and recognize the letter that represents that sound.
Hear and recognize in writing the difference between the short and long vowel sound.
Write the letter.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the Letter
• Point to the lowercase letter /a/ on the alphabet 
poster or on the board.
• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo emmi yunkuley yati jaat.   
Eciikaay uye yoo kayelak kooli yo /a/.  Wulaal 
búrom jiregaal: /a/
• Point to the lowercase letter /a/ on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo emmi yunkuley yati jaat. Eciikaay uye yoo kayelak kooli yo /a/. Wulaal 
búrom jiregaal: /a/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the uppercase letter "A" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo yákoney.  Yoo poop kayelak kooli yo /a/. Nampi etooŋumi ñetum di 
kasanken mba di karees, pan ujukaal man eciikimi eeno. 
• Point to the lowercase letter "a" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ñajuupoe, pan ujukaal man eciikimi eeno di furimaf.
• Say: Eciikay "a" eciika yaare, pan uliikenaal uyelaw wati siciikaas saaraas di kunoomak 
kabilewuumi.  Babaj  fúkawn  máamak man umanjaal siciikaas soololaal saaraas mati sibajoebajo 
di furimaf fanoofani fan uliikaalemi.

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap two-syllable words
• Say: Pan umiin furimaf man ubaj butingum furim. Butingum furim banoobani pan bubaj kayel 
kati eciikaay yaaraay, nan man uliikaami eeno - /awa/, /aba/.   Jileewaal man jijukaal.
• Model by clapping:   /a/ /wa/
• Practice together with pupils:  
• (awa= /a/ /wa/, aba= /a/, /ba/)
• Pupils practice alone: 

• (ajaŋa= /aja/, /ŋa/  atampa = /atam/, /pa/)
• Clap words with different numbers of syllables
• Say: Kurimak uke utingum ugaba kubaje,  bare furim fuŋ oolen-ŋoolen fubaj butingum bákon, 
utingum úfeejiir, mba wawuuje to.  Liikaal kurim kupinaay man ujukaal.  Ínje bee etooŋ  ireg 
furimaf.
• Ñaa jileewaalñagaba - síñakon.
Mata: ma/ta, babatak: ba/ba/tak

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Waawu  jijuke?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Jileewaal utingumaw wammi di kurimak Ñoone  butumbuu jijame kayelak /a/ di furimaf?
       (aba )? jileewaal inci.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or another language they 
know.
• Say: Jiregaal furimaf fabilewuumi - (awa).  Jijanjam kayelak kati eciikaay yaaraay di furimaf 
(awa)?  Ñoone butum buu jijame ko?
• Say: Ñaa karegawuul.  Jireg furimaf.  Nampi jilakomi eregey, jinen musinkam mooluul di 
fáteemenaaf fati eciikaay /a/ napi jiregumi kayelak /a/.
• Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Anoosani nanen jisinkaj joola di buwuloorumab  bati "balaab" tentemenaay. 
• Say: Waawu jijuke? Ure "balaab"
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Kayelak kati /a/ pan uŋoolen uñakaal ko.  Nampi  ulako'aami eregey yati ko, nuñakaal 
kayelak man kubaak. jijanjam kayelak kati eciikaay yaaraay /aa/ di furimaf: Balaab"?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two /a/ together, it makes a long sound /aa/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables and 
listen for the long vowel in the word.

activities.title: Writing – Letter
activities.content:
Write the letter and say its sound
• Write the letter /a/ on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm), and say its sound as you write. Pupils should then try it 
two more times while you watch and provide feedback.
• Demonstrate writing the letter on the chalkboard once more.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter 5 times

activities.title: How to read – using illustrations
activities.content:
Teach how to think about illustrations while 
reading
• Say: Di kajikerak kati uwuloorumaw  pan rambenolaal 
máamak man uliikaal wajuupoe mati bukanak di 
upanaw wammi di karegak. Jaat pan iliik kajareg.  
Nampi ulokowaami eliikey, pan uyiifaal jayinkun 
man úmikaal mati uwuloorumaaw wanaamutaw.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
eloley, éfohey, aluñooraaw
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils what they 
know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If needed, 
help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
• Read the following story aloud (use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if 
available)
• During reading, stop to discuss people and places
• Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, 
where they think the story takes place. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, what the characters 
like to do. Assure pupil responses are related to the pictures.
• Possible questions (use these, or ask your own questions):
• Where do you think they are? How do you know? What more can you say about that place?
• Who do you think this person is? What is he/she doing? 
• Talk about how the picture relates to parts of the story you are reading aloud.
Ensaa di Kurokaak Koola
No'ona nan pioe, Ensa di kalaakak koola nacine.
Fúnak fákon, namaj mati nawaarene añes bukan man kurokool di kalaakak koola.
Najawumi bee di eloley man aan yommi "Kajom ubil man urok di kalaakak kúmboom."
Eloley di yoonoomi, "Kaanujaat eyilooley let ebil, ínje pan ibil."  Ensaa nalaaŋenoomi, 
"A'aa, eyilooley let ebil."
najawumi bee baari eyilooley man aan yommi, "Kajom, ubil man urokom."  
Eyilooley di yommi, " Kaanujaat Éfohey pan ebil, ínje let ibil."  Ensaa aan yommi, 
"Háa a'aa! Éfohey let ebil."
Ensaa najawumi bee baari éfohey man aan yommi, "Kajom, ubil man urokom."  
Éfohey di yommi, "Kaanujaat aluñooraaw pan abil, ínje let ibil."  Ensaa naan yommi, 
"Háa a'aa! Aluñooraaw  let ebil."
Ensaa najawumi bee baari aluñooraaw  man aanoomi, "Kajom, ubil man urokom."  
Aluñooraaw naanoomi, "Kaanujaat eyelaay pan ebil, ínje let ibil."  Ensaa naanoomi, 
"Háa a'aa! Eyelaay let ebil."
Ensaa najawumi bee baari eyelaay man aan yommi, "Kajom, ubil man urokom."  
Eyelaay di yoonoomi, "Kaanujaat egoley pan ebil, ínje let ibil."  Ensaa naan yommi, 
"Háa a'aa! Egoley let ebil."
Ensaa najawumi bee baari egoley man aan yommi, "Kajom, ubil man urokom."  
Egoley di yoonoomi, "Kaanujaat sambunas  pan sibil, ínje let ibil."  Ensaa naan yommi, 
"Háa a'aa! sambunas let sibil."
Ensaa najawumi bee baari sambunas man aan sommi, "Kajom, ubil man urokom."  
Sambunas di soonoomi, "Kaanujaat emitey pan elub, ínje let ibil."  
Ensaa naan yommi, "Háa a'aa! emitey let elub."
Fati kajomey di bújomoreey, koo búrom di kujawumi bee di kalaakak kati Ensaa
Eyilooley di eforumi eloley.
Éfohey di ekosoorumi eyilooley di  muciwam mooli yo.
Aluñooraaw nayahumi éfohey
Eyelaay di epitumi aluuñooraaw.
Egoley di ebujumi eyelaay.
Sambunas di sireemenumi egoley.
Kalubak di kufokumi sambunas.
Ñaa Ensaa nárupo sút jíteyej

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3 pupils at random to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in 
their own words. Ask pupils how the word was used in the story.
• Say: Jiŋaraal kurimak kan  uliikenulaami man ujoonenaal kasanken kunkul
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil book 
or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a new 
sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the pupils, 
depending on the responses.

• Ban naceeŋ ume waawu?

• When you find the picture that has the vowel sound, have pupils connect the picture to the

• For the second set of pictures, focus on the long vowel sound.

activities.title: Sight word review
activities.content:
Review the sight words from last week 
• Say: Di funoomaf fawuujumi nuliikaaliik ureesaw wati áriiŋaaw di ámajiraaw wan ootaale ejuk 
nanoosani di uliikenaw.  Jiwoolowoolo kareeesak kati ámajiraaw?  Di kareesak kati áriiŋaaw?
• Write the two sight words (Kaddy and Buba) on the board.
• Call on 10 pupils randomly to come to the board, one at a time. Say the names of the boy 
and girl randomly.  See if pupils can point to the correct name when you call it out. If so, 
congratulate them. If not, help them by having them point at each one, and repeat the correct 
name with you. Then try again with the same student to be sure he or she knows the word.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Review the question word "bóbey" ("Nóney") 
• Read the question: 
• Where did Ensaa Live? Ensaa bóbey nacine?  
• Answer: (karamba káamak). Ensaa di kalaakak koola nacine.)
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Say: "Mante jijanjam furimaf fan uŋaraami man uceeŋaal kúceeŋak wan uliikenulaami kunak 
kupinaay bálamuk?"
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "where" asks us about a place)

• Teach pupils to use the question word "when" ("Nóney/nampi") 
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "when". Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: "When do you like to play outside? 
• Say: "Nóney jimaŋemi fáreedaf téeŋeey?"
• Call on 2 pupils to answer. Their answer should be a time (i.e. in the morning, after school, on 
the weekend)
• Say: Furimaf ("Nóney wan fufelumi") mati baŋaanab fuceeŋemi.  Nampi ijammi "nóney," 
nimanj mati kulaaŋenak pan kukaan baŋaanab.  Pan ŋoolem kaan baŋaan di funakaf (nan 
bújomoreey), funakaf fati di funoomaf (nan Fubeten), mba baŋaan di emitey (nan di 
fujamaray).
• Read the question: Ensaa nóney namaŋe man kurokaak kurambenool di kalaakak koola?
• Answer: Say: Ñaa uwoonooraal wan uliikulaami.  Karegak koone:
• Ask pupils to think about when, or the time, that this happened. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Ay  aciibe épimbeney éfohey? 
• Answer: Kúlaaŋenak: Aluñooraaw aciibe épimbeney bee di éfohey.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. 
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Evaluate pupils use of the keyword "when" ("TRANSLATE")
• Say: Furimaf ("Nóney wan fufelumi") mati baŋaanab fuceeŋemi.  Nampi ijammi "nóney," di jimanj 
mati kulaaŋenak pan kukaan baŋaanab.  Pan ŋoolem kaan baŋaan di funakaf (nan bújomoreey), 
funakaf fati di funoomaf (nan Fubeten), mba baŋaanab di emitey (nan di fujamaray).
• Read the question:
• Question: "Nóney Ensaa amaŋumi man kurokaak kurambenool di kalaakak koola?"
• Answer:  Ensaa kajom namaŋumi man kurokaak  koola kurambenool.
• Say: Ñaa uwoonooraal wan uliikulaami.  Karegak koone: "Kajom jibil jirokom."  Kuregireg nóney 
bajoe.

Review the question word "where" ("bóbey"), "who" ("ayima") and "when" ("nóney")

question word "where" asks us the name of someone or something alive)

• Answer:  Áfanlumaw di bítikey najawe enoomey yati usamataaw.
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Continue by reviewing what each keyword is asking about, and then ask the question.
• Say: "Ay" (Eceeŋowolaal ceeŋ man ulaaŋenaal ñetum banab mba di búkaanum)

• Say: "Nóney" (yoo eceeŋolaal ñetum di baŋaam mba funakaf)

• Say: Áfanlumaw nóney najuke usamataaw wan alakomi eñesey?

mba di karees, pan ujukaal man eciikimi eemo.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Waawu jijuke?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Jileewaal uñenaw woololaal man siriiboor di butingumab ji/cees. Ñoone  butumbuu jijame 
/i/ di furimak " jicees?" Jilaañaal uleewaal inci.  
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another language 
they know.
• Say: Jilaañaal jiregaal furimaf fábilewuumi.  Furimaf fabilewuumi foo emmi "kabik."   Jijanjam 
kayelak /i/ di furimaf "kabik"  ñoone butum buu jijame ko?" 
• Say: Ñaa karegaak kooli.  Reg furimaf.  Nampi ulakomi eregey, nen  jisinkaj jooli di 
fáteemenaaf fati eciikaay /i/ nampi uregumi kayelak kooli yo.
• Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Everyone should place their finger under the first picture at the bottom. What do you 
see? 
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Anoosani nanen jisinkaj joola di fáteemenaaf fati buwuloorumab butooŋandab.  Waawu 
jijuke?  Ure doo emmi "miil''
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
(Answer: two)
• Tell pupils that when they see two "i" together, it makes a long sound /ii/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables 
and listen for the long vowel in the word.

Umpa di ejaameney
Umpa di fiilaf foola kucine tákon.  Kubabaj sikumba sigaba, siyilool sífeejiir, ébe yákon, di 
ejaameen.  Ejaameney yoo efuurifuuri máamak.  Mukaanaam mooli yo mafuuriyaam mukaanekaan 
man Umpa aha lúu.
Fúnak fákon, Umpa bajuke ejaameney di ekaan mukaanaay majakut.  Natey areg inaa oola.  Bare 
inaa oola oomu man asofoe di burokab.  Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat eregey yati uregaw." Natey bee 
baari baa oola.  Bare baa oola poop oomu man asofoe di burokab.   Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat eregey 
yati uregaw.  "Natey bee baari átumbewool ániinaaw.  Bare átumbewool ániinaaw poop oomu man 
asofoe di burokab. Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat eregey yati uregaw." 
Natey bee baari áliinool. Bare áliinool poop oomu man asofoe di burokab. Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat

baari baa oola.  Bare baa oola poop oomu man asofoe di burokab.   Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat eregey 
yati uregaw.  "Natey bee baari átumbewool ániinaaw.  Bare átumbewool ániinaaw poop oomu man 
asofoe di burokab. Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat eregey yati uregaw." 
Natey bee baari áliinool. Bare áliinool poop oomu man asofoe di burokab. Nammi, "Hée Umpa, kat

• "Waawu," jimanj mati kalaaŋenak pan kukaan waaf wan oote ejuk mba nugor, mba di kaan waaf 
wápjuloe.

kareesak kati énukuruŋey.  Nampi iceeŋumi, "waawu?"  Nimammaŋ bee emanj wan wahaw

bab, eloja, biibii, baaba, eyen, kabik

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "b" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say:  Eciikaay uye yoo emmi yunkuley yati jaat /b/. Eciikaay kayelak kooliyo /b/. 
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "B" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo yákoney.  Yoo poop kayelak kooli yo /b/.  Nampi etooŋumi  ñetum di 
kasanken mba di karees, pan ujukaal man eciikimi eemo. 
• Point to the small letter "b" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ñajuupoe pan ujukaal yo mo'ome di kurimak.

Keyword picture study   
• Say: Waawu jijuke?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Wulaal búrom uregaal furimaf/bab/. Jijanjam kayelak /b/ di furimaf /bab/?  
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
• Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
Point to the keyword.
• Say: /bab/.
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of the 
keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the  "b"
• Say: Kayel kéy ebaje? (pupils respond) "Eciikaay yunkuley "b"
• Cover the "b" and show the "a" (pupils respond "a"
• Say: Kayel kéy ebaje? 
• Kuniilak di kulaaŋen ("a")
• Say: Jiliik uyelaw káon kákon, jibanujaat di jinampem uyelaw man jibaj butingum furim.  Ñaa 
jireg furimaf bapajulut uyelaw. /b/, /a/ "ba"
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
• Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3) 
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: "Jíyenten jak man jijiker.  Ínje bee eliik utingum kurim ibanujaa ninampen  wo man ibaj 
furim"
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Wulaal búrom uraagalaal.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
reading the same word by themselves. 
• Say: Ñaa numanjaamanj wan ootaami ekaaney.  Wulaal bee eliik kurim kuceen di sibukaas 
sooluul nan man uliikulaami eeno.  Jimond jiliik utingumaw, jibanujaat di jireg furimaf.  Jiŋar 
musinkam mooluul man jiriiben.  (kooñaam ban nuramben kuñiilak.)

activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Aseekaw bañuure jisinkaj kábabubaak. Waawu ukaane? Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. Do NOT read it aloud for them. They 
should whisper read (read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If 
pupils finish reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have learnt to read 
words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to remember the predictions they made before they read the story. Give them a 
moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what happened in the 
story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. Ask the pupils 
if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to locate the letter"b" in a word in the decodable story. Call on 2 pupils at random to 
share the words they found.
• Write the letter "b" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you do it. Invite 
pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "b" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with the sound 
/b/.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check predictions based on title
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupil predicted before the read aloud. Ask the pupils if his 
prediction matched what was in the story.
• Ask the other pupils to think about what they predicted. Call on 2 pupils at random. Ask what 
they predicted, why, and if what they predicted is what happened in the story.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their own 
words.
• Say: "Jiŋaraal kurimak kan uliikenulaami man ujoonenaal usanken wunkul."
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil book 
or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a new 
sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the pupils, 
depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. Encourage pupils to 
share the words with their families at home.

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. List 
all the pupils in the class in alphabetical order. 
Then make 3 more columns with the title "letters", 
"syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who decodable story for this lesson. Instruct pupils who are not being assessed to read 
the story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual pupils.
• Say: Di bújom bákon kuniilak bajawe eñes waaf di karambaak bare umanjutaal waawu kujawe 
       eñes. Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal.
•  Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils starting 
with the next pupil on the list.

• Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general sense 
of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate that the child 
is struggling. 
• Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 40-50 is 
good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement activities for 
skill areas that are less than 40.
• Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound.Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllableson the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Furimaf ufe waawu fufele?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: ínje ombo niwoonoore furim. Furimaf fucila: "ababe." Jileewaal síñakon "/a/ /ba/ /be/"
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Furimaf ufe "ababe." Ñaa nubanaaban eciikey yati kurimak búrom. Wulaal búrom uliikaal 
       síñakon.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the syllables 
of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their copy 
books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest of the 
words.
• Words: Enter words that can be made by syllables in the Pupil Book
• Abi: A/bi, kaboob: ka/boob, baa/ba: baaba, ka/bik: kabik
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Now, I want you to try if you can form your own words!
• Say: Ñaa nimammaŋ man jiliik mante pan jiŋoolen  jijoonen kurim kooluul.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know and 
write it in their copy books.
• When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a partner to share the word they made.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter

• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo emmi yunkuley yati jaat. Eciikaay uye kayelak kooli yo /k/.  Wulaal búrom 
uregaal: /k/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "K" on the alphabet poster or on the board.

• Say: "Eciikaay uye yoo yákoney.  Yoo poop kayelak kooli yo /k/.  Nampi etooŋumi  ñetum di furim 
mba di karees, pan ujamaal di eyel mo'omu." 
• Point to the small letter "k" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ñajuupoe pan ujukaal yo mo'ome di kurimak.
• Keyword picture study  
• Say: Waawu jijuke?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Wulaal búrom uregaal furimaf/kaboobak/. Jijanjam kayelak /k/ di furimaf /kaboobak/? 
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Fúkaaf fati furimaf "kaboobak"
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of the 
keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2) 
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "k"
• Say: Kayel kéy ebaje? (pupils respond kuñiilak di kureg "a").  
• Cover the "k" and show the "a"
• Say: Kayel kéy ebaje? (pupils respond kuñiilak di kureg "a"). 
• Say: Jiregaal uyelaw síñakon man jibajaal utingum kurim. Ñaa, jiliikaal utingum kurim síñakon 
       /ka/
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
• Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it. 

4. Read syllables (5 mins)
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Jíyenten jak man jijiker.  Ínje bee eliik utingum kurim ibanujaat ninampen wo man ibaj 
furim.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Wulaal búrom uregaal síñakon.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: Ñaa jimanjaamanj wan jootaami ekaaney.  Jikaan mo'omu mákonam man jiliik kurimak di 
sibukaas sooluul nan man uliikulaami eeno.  Jimond jiliik utingumaw, jibanujaat di jireg furimaf.  
Jiŋar musinkam mooluul man jiriiben.  (kooñaam ban nuramben kuñiilak.
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

Faatu di Kaleeŋak
Faatu jijaŋa jayinkun jan umanje nanoosani súumesúum jo.
Jíreediyereedi di sínukuruŋas sanaamutas, utojaw, sikoobaas, kujaŋaak, di wanoosani wan  jijukumi 
di karegak.
Bare wan afaŋumi man amaŋe man kúreedi woo emmi kaleeŋak.  Namaŋemaŋ bee esof ko, bare 
áŋooleneriit.
Naremboorumi di búbaar babaake man asof mati uñenaw woola pan utook kaleeŋak, bare utookut.  
Nanenumi kásiyak kati mumelam lóy man ajiker dó yáalindaay yati kaleeŋak.
Najawumi bee di kalimbisak koola, bare najukumi mati kaleeŋak kuneemooneemoor!  Najikerumi di 
ejuudoorumaay, nájukudomi kaleeŋ kuceen!  Bare namanjumi mati kaleeŋ kákon ceb kubajoe.
Nan kaleeŋak kúpurulomi ceb, di sálowoomi.
Náruudenumi di bacaacool mante baa oola ajamool.
Najawulomi bee di kalimbisak.
Baa ooal naceeŋoomi, "añiilaw úmboom Faatu, waa núruudene di "Iŋoolenut isof kaleeŋak!"
Baa oola naanoomim "Let uŋoolen usof kaleeŋak.  Wampi uŋoolenumi usof woo eenomi yáalindaay 
yooli ko.
Faatu nasof mati sáalinda sajuupoe soombo.  Ban kuñiil kajuupoe pan kuŋoolen kúreedi di so.
Nammi, "Moo jajak. Kama kaleeŋak bukanak búrom kucile ko.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils starting 
with the next pupil on the list.
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general sense 
of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate that the child 
is struggling. 

Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 40-50 is 
good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement activities for 
skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE:
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blendi
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have 
learned bi t need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. 
Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 
5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter. 
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound that 
pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap the 
letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already learned. 
*TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, 
then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly.
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to use 
letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its sound. 
Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to 
turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on 
the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. 
Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call one 
of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down raises 
their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their copy

• /ka/ba / = kaba, /ka/boob/ = kaboob, /ka/bik/= kabik, e/ bab/ = abab

sound in a few different words.
Jiyela Jayinkun   
Lakomi, lakomi, di lakomi tokos. Bajembaj feh fákon fayinkun. Fabeti tentaamey di mafosam. 
Funak fákon fehaf di fufenkumi jiyela yayinkun di jípurulomi. Jiylaaj joo ceb jo.
Di jijegoorooroomi, nan jijikerumi fatiyaay, di jijukumi jiilaj jati esuwaay. Jiñiilaj jati esuwaay di 
jommi, "Háa! Jiyela, aw juuderutey." Jiyelaaj di jiceeŋoomi "Waawu wajuuderutumi di
ínje?" Jiñiilaj jati esuwaay di jommi, "Aw ubajut ulega mba úsit." Jiyelaaj jayinkunaaj di jommi, 
"Háa! Waawu niwaarene ikaan man ibaj dooru?" Jiñiilaj jati esuwaay di jommi, "Bonket, ujaw 
uceeŋ kápentiripentak, "di jijukumi kápentiripentak, kápentiripentak kati kúpaarankuun kajake, 
kakote di búbaarab. Kápentiripentak di kommi jiyelaaj, "Háa! Jiyela aw juuderutey, jiyelaaj di 
jiceeŋukomi, "Waawu wajuuderutumi di ínje?" Kápentiripentak di kommi, "aw ubajut ulega
mba úsit ban jaat let uŋoolen úyiit." Jiyelaaj di jiceeŋumi, kaanujaat eeno mo waawu niwaarene 
ikaa?" Di koonujomi, jaw uceeŋ efooley. "Ñaa jiyelaaj di jífuuloorumi jijaw eñesey yati efooley. 
Jiyelaaj di jíriiŋumi di fuuyaaf. "Di jijukumi jifoolaj man jilakoe di ekoobaay. Jifoolaf jijikerumi jo 
ban di jommi, "Háa, jiyela aw juuderutey. "Jiyelaaj di jiceeŋumi, "Waawu wajuuderutumi di
ínje?" Jifoolaj di jommi aw ubajut úkamun banjaat let uŋoolen urend nan ínje." Jiyelaaj di jommi, 
kamma ñaa waawu niwaarene ikaan?" Tootootoo, ekubey di épurulomi di fuuyaaf. Di ejikerumi 
jiyelaaj di yommi, "Aw ay maŋ?" Jiyelaaj di joonuyomi, "ínje imanjut! Wan imanjumi woo eenomi 
ínje juuderutey." Ekubey di yoonujomi, "Háa! A'aa. Bonket úfuuloor ulaañ bóot man ujaw uñes 
inaa ooli." Ñaa jiyelaaj di jífuuloorumi jilaañ bee ban jípurulomi di fehaf fooli jo. Nan jíriigumi
to, di jijukumi énukuruŋ yan jijukurerut. Waaf wabaake uban di ukuur, ban di ubaj kunaab kula di 
kútumpaay, ban poop fúredimpaf fooli wo di fubaakumi. Di wommi, "Háa, jiñiilaj júmboom jiyelaaj! 
Bóbey nujee?" Jiyelaaj di jísalo. Di kammi eyela! Kaanut waaf wajuuderuti. Ceeŋut man jibaj úsit, 
mba ulega, mba úkamun. Ceeŋut man jíyiit mba di jirend nan efool. Waafaw búrom jibaje. Joo 
jiyela

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the 
title "letters", "syllables" and "individual 
score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find 
the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who are not being assessed to read the 
story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Babaj ániine ákon di aseek ákon man kurookoe uktekelaw, bare umanjutaal waawu 
wóndo. Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending". 
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call one 
of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down raises 
their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Furimaf ufe waawu fufele?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Ínje ombo kawoonoor furim.  Furim fucila "biitab." Jileewaal fo: /bii/tab/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Furim ufe "biitab." Ñaa  wulaal  búrom nubajaabaj furim faciiki.  Jiliikaal síñakon.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the syllables 
of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their copy 
books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest of the 
words.
• Words: katik, biitab, batebe, baaba, bati 
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Ñaa nimammaŋ man jiliikooro kajoonenak kati kurimak kooluul.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know and 
write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:

Keyword picture study

• Say: Wulaal búrom uregaal: "n" jijanjam kayelak "n" di furimaf "Nabi"
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.

Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Furimaf [Nabi].
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.

syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "N". 
• Say: Kayelak uke kéy? (kuñiilak di kulaaŋen "N")
• Cover the "n"and also cover and show the "a".
• Say: Kayelak uke kéy? (kuñiilak di kulaaŋen "a" 
• Cover the "Na" and show the "bi".
• Say: Kayelak uke kéy? (kuñiilak di kulaaŋen "bi") 
• Say: Jireg uyelaw síñakon, jibanujaat di jinampen man jireg butingum furim. Ñaa jireg uyelaw 
• síñakon /Na/ /bi/ /Nabi/.
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
• Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Jíyentenoor ban di jijiker.  Ínje bee eliik utingum kurim ban ninampen wo man ikaan wo 
furim.  
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Jiliikaal síñakon
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: (Kooñaam ban nuramben kuñiilak)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently

quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If pupils finish reading early, 
they can read the story again with a partner.

read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words.

Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "n" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, ask them to draw a picture of something that begins with the 
sound /n/.

Read the following story aloud again (use the pictures in it while reading)

pupils struggled with one of the new vocabulary words, pause to discuss its meaning in the

Joon di Méeri
Funak fákon, Joon áyitaaliwut. Joon baa oola, Baa Pool nammi, "Joon aw mante ootut bee ejaw 
di fuliitikenaf jaat" Joon naanoomi, "Wúli balooke buruŋab." Joon nawaakewnumi atey anoken 
di sijaamenas di sisahaas. Nawaakenumi ajaw ámukenul kehak. Joon atiyool Méeri, najawumi 
aramben Joon, man kuwunumi Sinukuruŋas furiaf. Méeri nasenumi siyiloolas
síkontiboobas. Joon nasenumi sijaamenas di sisahaas étuureey. Sínukuruŋas di sitooŋumi ekaan 
búlok bati kásuumaay. Méeri di súumoomi. Nammi, "Sínukuruŋas súnsuum so máamak!" Méeri 
naceeŋumi Joon, usenutaal jaat sínukuruŋas furiaf, waawu woote esof so?" Joon naanoomi, 
"Soo bee ecet. Wulaal ootaale kacookoor so man siroŋ. Joon narunlen di aan, soo sínukuruŋ san 
kukure." "Kaanenujaat nan soo sínukuruŋ sati karamba saanomi nan siñaabas di sibonkas, soo 
pan sicookoorooro." "Bare sijaamenas, sisahaas di siyiloolas soololaal soo wulaal ootaale esenso 
furiaf, mumelam di fufintaf." Joon di Méeri inaa ooliil nabilumi. Naaniimi, "Jicookoocookoor 
sínukuruŋas jak. Súusuum so, ban wulaal poop súumolaasuum."
3. Comprehension - Factual & inferential questions (10 mins)
Ask factual questions
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer the following question:
      Question: Joon di Méeri waawu kucookooremi? 
      FACTUAL QUESTION Sijaamenas di sisahaas kucookooremi.  Read that sentence. 
• After the response, congratulate, help, or correct the pupil's answer. If the pupil is partly 
correct or incorrect, tell them why. Help pupils find the sentence in the story that contains the 
answer.
• Ask inferential questions
• Ask each of the following questions. 
      Question 1 INFERENTIAL QUESTION. Waawu ukaane man Joon kulook buruŋab? 
      POSSIBLE ANSWERS: Mambi kuŋoolen kusof sínukuruŋas. 
      Question 2: INFERENTIAL QUESTION. Joon kehak kan amukenumi waawu nakaane ko?  
      POSSIBLE ANSWERS:  Balake man kutokoñ 
• After each question, pupils talk in pairs about their answers. Call on a pupil randomly to share 
their answer to the question. Discuss their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about 
what is in the text or picture, as well as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have 
given them that idea.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "n" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Uye eciikaay yoololaal yunkuley.  Eciikaay kayelak kooli yo /n/. Wulaal  búrom uregaal: 
/n/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "N" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo yákoney.  Yoo poop kayelak kooli yo /n/. Nampi etoo¿umi  ñetum di 
kasanken mba di karees, pan ujukaal man eciikeyimi di eeno. 
• Point to the small letter "n" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ñajuupoe di kurimak, pan ujukaal yo mo'ome.

Keyword picture study
• Say: Waawu jijuke?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Wulaal búrom uregaal: "n". Jijanjam kayelak /n/ di furimaf "Nabi"
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
• Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: The keyword is "Nabi"
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "n".
• Say: Kayelak uke kéy? (kuñiilak di kulaaŋen "n")
• Cover the "n" and show the "a".
• Say: Kayelak uke kéy? (kuñiilak di kulaaŋen "a") 
• Say: Jireg uyelaw síñakon, jibanujaat di jinampen wo man jireg butingum furim.  Ñaa jireg 
uyelaw síñakon /n/ a/ /na/.
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Jíyentenoor ban di jijiker.  Ínje bee eliik utingum kurim ban ninampen wo man ikaan wo 
furim.  
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Jiliikaal síñakon.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: Ñaa jimamanj wan jootumi ekaaney.  Jikaan mo'omu mákonam man jiliik kurimak di 
síbukaas sooluul.  Jimond jiliik utingum kurim ban di jireg furimaf.  Jiŋar musinkam mooluul 
man  jiñuur jiriiben wan jommi di eliikey.
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.
