activities.title: My language
activities.content:
Teach a rule of the language 
• Help pupils to find my language picture box in 
the Pupil's Book
• Say: Nampi ulako'aami kasankenak 
mba káyentenoorak kati kurimak mba kasanken 
di fúrerempaf foololaal, babaj sílinga san 
ceeŋumi man uriibenaal.  
Sílingaas use soo sirambenemi bukaaku man kúlawul máamak wanoowani wan wulaal mba 
bukaaku kuregewoolaami.  Jaat jíyentenooraal waaf wunkul wákon.
• Say:  Waawu jijuke di buwuloorumab?
• Say: ínje bee ereg furim mba niliik kasanken.  Jíyentenoor jak. 
• Sibukaas sooliil.
• sibukaas súmboom.
• sibukaas sooli.

• Illustration: A picture of a woman giving food to a woman
• Say: Waawu núlawulumi mati furimaf mba kasanken? Waawu  fufele?  (kurimak kúfeejiirak uke  
kúyisenyisen waaf wan bukan kucile. Kasankenak kutooŋandak kúyisenyisen mati waaf wan 
bukan kucile.  Kasankenak kugabutak kúyisenyisen mati waaf wan ínje kucile.  Kasankenak 
kúfeejitak kúyisenyisen mati waaf wan aw kucile.)
• Say: Kasanken kéy kúyisenumi wan ujukaami di buwuloorumab?
• Call 1-2 learners to give similar example of my language rule and explain what it means. Focus

Joon di Méeri
Funak fákon, Joon áyitaaliwut. Joon baa oola, Baa Pool nammi, "Joon aw mante ootut bee ejaw 
di fuliitikenaf jaat" Joon naanoomi, "Wúli balooke buruŋab." Joon nawaakewnumi atey anoken 
di sijaamenas di sisahaas. Nawaakenumi ajaw ámukenul kehak. Joon atiyool Méeri, najawumi 
aramben Joon, man kuwunumi Sinukuruŋas furiaf. Méeri nasenumi siyiloolas
síkontiboobas. Joon nasenumi sijaamenas di sisahaas étuureey. Sínukuruŋas di sitooŋumi ekaan 
búlok bati kásuumaay. Méeri di súumoomi. Nammi, "Sínukuruŋas súnsuum so máamak!" Méeri 
naceeŋumi Joon, usenutaal jaat sínukuruŋas furiaf, waawu woote esof so?" Joon naanoomi, 
"Soo bee ecet. Wulaal ootaale kacookoor so man siroŋ. Joon narunlen di aan, soo sínukuruŋ san 
kukure." "Kaanenujaat nan soo sínukuruŋ sati karamba saanomi nan siñaabas di sibonkas, soo 
pan sicookoorooro." "Bare sijaamenas, sisahaas di siyiloolas soololaal soo wulaal ootaale esenso 
furiaf, mumelam di fufintaf." Joon di Méeri inaa ooliil nabilumi. Naaniimi, "Jicookoocookoor 
sínukuruŋas jak. Súusuum so, ban wulaal poop súumolaasuum."

activities.title: Assessment: Before the Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the title 
"letters", "syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find 
the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who are not being assessed to read the 
story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Nabi bababe kábabumaak ban umanjutaal waawu ukaane man abab.  Jiliikaal karegak 
man jimanjaal.  
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your 
pupils found challenging in the assessment. The 
skill reinforced by the activity is in the activity 
name: "letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Furimaf ufe waawu fufele?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Ínje ombo kawoonoor furim.  Furim fucila "Nabi." Jileewaal fo: /na/bi/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Furim fucila "Nabi." Ñaa wulaal poop nubajaabaj furim faciiki. Jiliikaal síñakon.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Babaj waaf waliile di karambaak di kapanak kati baalab, bare umanjutaal waaf wanoe 
buu. Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal.
• Click or tap here to enter text.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound.Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with the 
sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound that 
pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap the 
letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already learned. 
*TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, 
then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to use 
letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its sound. 
Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to 
turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the flashcards. When they agree on the 
syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call 
on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue 
using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call one 
of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down raises 
their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story

book. Read the first word.
• Say: Furimaf ufe waawu fufele?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Ínje ombo nawoonoore furim. Furimaf foo emmi "Balen"
• Frimaf foo emmi "Balen". Ñaa jifasaal fo ban nuleewaa fo: "Balen"
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Furim fucila "Balen."  Ñaa nuciikaaciik furimaf búrom. Ñaa jiliikaal síñakon.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the 
rest of the words.
• Words: Balen, Laaloo, lako, leeb, baalab, elab 
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Ñaa nimammaŋ man muyuul  jiliikoorro man jijuk mante pan  jiŋoolen jijoonen kurim 
kooluul. Ñaa nimammaŋ man jijoonero kurimak kooluul.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

Erohaay di Awañaaw
No`ona nan pioe awañaw Baara nacineene.
Funak oo funak, narokerok máamak di kalaakak koola.
Nalukeluk sisaanaas.  Sisaanaas siliiliil jak.

Nawunewun sisaanaas anoosani - nawunewun áyiaw anaaraaw di ániinaaw poop. Funak fákon

activities.title: Assessment: Before the lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the 
title "letters", "syllables" and "individual 
score".

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Funak fákon bajuke áriiŋaaw man ajuume man aaken waaf di kañenak koola, bare 
umanjutaal waawu naakene.  Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have 
learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter 
sound. 
• Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their 
words, then move on to the next letter.    
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Furimaf ufe waawu fufele ?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: ínje ombo nawoonoore furim. Furimaf fucila: "jala." Jileewaal síñakon "/ja//la/"
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Furimaf ufe "jala." Ñaa nubanaaban eciikey yati kurimak búrom. Wulaal búrom uliikaal 
• síñakon
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the 
rest of the words.
• Words: jala, jaba, jibekel, jaleebaj 
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Ñaa nimammaŋ man jiliik mante pan jiŋoolen jijonen kurim kooluul.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

Listening game - first sound
• Say each word below. Pupils put a hand up if they hear the sound in the word and on the 
desk if they do not.
• maala, moola, bateme, etem, miin, melam, moj, mat

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "m"on the alphabetposter or on the board.
• Say: Eciikaay uye yoo emmi yunkuley yati jaat.  Eciikay uye kayelak kooli yo /m/.  Wulaal 
búrom uregaal: /m/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "M" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: "Eciikaay uye yoo yákoney.  Yoo poop kayelak kooli yo /m/.  Nampi etooŋumi ñetum di 
furim mba di karees, pan ujamaal di eyel mo'omu." 
• Point to the small letter "m" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ñajuupoe pan ujukaal yo mo'ome di kurimak

Keyword picture study
• Say: Waawu jijuke?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Wulaal búrom uregaal furimaf maala". Jijanjam kayelak /m/ di furimaf "maala"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: The word is /maala /.
• Say: Furimaf foo emmi "maala"
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "m".
• Say: Kayel kéy ebaje? (pupils respond kuñiillak di kulaaŋen "m")
• Cover the "m" and show the "a".
• Say: Kayel kéy ebaje? (pupils respond kuñiillak di kulaaŋen "a")\
• Say: Jiregaal uyelaw síñakon man jibajaal utingum kurim.  Ñaa, jiliikaal utingum kurim síñakon 
/m/ /a/ /ma/ 
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: "Jijanten jak ban di jijiker. Ínje bee eliik butingum furim ban ninampen man ibaj furim."
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Wulaal búrom jiregaal síñakon.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: Ñaa jimamanj wan jootaami ekaaney. Jikaan mo'omu mákonam man jiliik kurimak di 
• síbukaas sooluul nan man uliikulaami eeno. Jimond jiliik utingumaw, jibanujaat di jireg 
• furimaf. Jiŋar musinkam mooluul man jiriiben. (kooñaam ban nuramben kuñiilak.  
• Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

the Pupil's Book. .

bukaaku man kúlawul máamak wanoowani 
wan ulaal mba bukaaku kuregewoolaami. Jaat 
jíyentenooraal waaf wunkul wákon.

• Síbukaas soosu di taabuley.
• Síbukaas soosu di fáteemenaaf. 
• Síbukaas soosu bajam di taabuley.

• Say: Waawu núlawulumi mati kasanken?  Waawu kufele?  (kurimak kúfeejiirak uke  kúyisenyisen 
tan wahaw wommi. Kasankenak kutoo ŋandak kúyisenyisen mati wahaw woowu di taabuley.  
Kasankenak kugabutak kúyisenyisen mati wahaw woowu di fáteemenaaf fati tabuuley.  
Kasankenak kúfeejitak kúyisenyisen mati wahaw woowu di bajam di taabuley.)
• Say: Kasanken kéy kúyisenumi wan ujukaami di buwuloorumab?
• Call 1-2 learners to give similar example of my language rule and explain what it means. Focus 
on my language examples in pupils'examples.

activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Write the vocabulary on the board (but not the definitions). Ask pupils what they know 
about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know. 
• etem  abonket

activities.title: Comprehension - Prediction
activities.content:
Prediction based on picture
• Help pupils find the decodable text of the day in their Pupil Books by holding up the page and 
saying the page number.
• Say: "Look at this picture! What do you see? What do you think this story will be about?"
• Say: "Jijker buwuloorumab ube.  Waawu jijuke?  Waawu jisofumi woo wootumi kabajo'aak di 
karegak?"
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a partner. Call 
on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Ñaa, muyuul cebuul joote ereg karegak di síbukaas sooluul.  Jiliik kurimak kammi di 
karegak mati koo nuciikulaami di kurimak kan uliikenulaami.
• Say: Bajuke kujaŋa kugaba man kulakoe di ejunkut, nuwoonoor waawu kombo di ekaan.  Ñaa 
Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal. 
• Say: Jiŋar wan jimanjumi di siciikaas man uliikooro karegak. Nampi jilakomi eliikey di jiŋar 
musinkam mooluul man jiriiben furim fanoosani.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. Do NOT read it aloud for them. They 
should whisper read (read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If 
pupils finish reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have learnt to 
read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to remember the predictions they made before they read the story. Give them a 
moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what happened in the 
story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. Ask the 
pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
Pupils practice writing the letter

random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter " m " on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you do it. 
Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "m" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with the sound 
/m/.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:

• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such 
as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learnt or when you hear a syllable the 
pupils just practiced.
Kasiitiilak di Ejaameney
Di funak fákon balaab man búbolie, ejaameney di kasiitiilak baraanab basofe so mámaak. 
Ejaameney di yommi, "Ujaal uñesaal mumelam man uraanaal."
Kasiitiilak di kumaŋumi di kommi, "Éey jaal man uñesaal." Di sijawumi, sijawumi, sijawumi
Di siteyumi, siteyumi, siteyumi.
Di múlamukaam di síriiŋumi di fumojaf (koloŋey).
Ejaameney di yommi, "Ñaa pan ubajaal mumelam man uraanaal!" 
Kasiitiilak di kumaŋumi, "Éey pan ubajaal mumelam man uraanaal."
Kasiitiilak di kubaalumi éloro di fumojaf (koloŋey). 
Ejaameney poop di ebaalumi éloro di fumojaf (koloŋey).
Kasiitiilak di kuraanumi mumelam - kuraan kuraan kuraan. 
Ejaameney poop di eraanumi mumelam - eraan, eraan, eraan. 
Di siraanumi mante soo búrom sipooñ.
Ñaa épuruley di ériiŋumi.
Kasiitiilak di kommi, "Fumojaf (Koloŋey) ésenkisenki, ínje let iŋoolen ípurul."
Ejaameney poop di emaŋumi, Éey, fumojaf (koloŋey) ésenkisenki. Ínje let iŋoolen ípurul! Buu 
nootaale ekaan?"
Kasiitiilak di kommi, ñaa ínje nimammanj buu nootaale ekaan eeno. Ínje pan imond iremboor di 
bálamukab booli man ípur. Nampi ípurumi, ínje pan iñakuli ípurenli."
Ñaa kasiitiilak di kaanumi moomu man kúpurulomi. Ejaameney di ewonkumi, "Jasiitiil, aw óomey" 
Bare kasiitiilak koo kumaamaal kábíñooney.
Di piyo jasinkun, jijaŋa yayinkun di jíjawulomi bee di fumojaf (koloŋey), di jijam ejaameen dihi elok 
di fumojaf (koloŋey).  Jijaŋaaj di jirambenumi ejaameney man épurul di fumojaf (koloŋey).

Ejaameeney di esalumi jijaŋaaj ban di emaŋ bee ejaw. Too galab, di ejukumi kasiitiilak di fulatenaf.  
Kasiitiilak di kommi, "Jajaameen, bonket úyolen kaneyaak di kumerak kúmboom kammojaat niŋoolen 
igoren fúkaaf fúmboom manoosani."
Ejaameney di elaaŋenoomi, "Éey, pan irambeni. Bare aw poop foo uliiken buruŋ bajoone ban oote 
karamben apaali."

activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.

words.
• "Jiŋaraal kurimak kan uliitikenulaami man ujoonenaal usanken wuceem."
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - a sentence that is not in the 
pupil book or read aloud.
• For each of the other vocabulary words introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word 
in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct 
the pupils, depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. Encourage pupils to 
share the words with their families at home.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Write the vocabulary on the board (but not the definitions). Ask pupils what they know about 
each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.

      kajinlene

activities.title: Comprehension - Prediction
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Help pupils find the decodable text of the day in their Pupil Books by holding up the page and 
saying the page number.
• Say: Jijker buwuloorumab ube.  Waawu jijuke?  Waawu jisofumi woo wootumi kabajo'aak di 
karegak?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a partner. Call 
on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Ñaa, muyuul cebuul joote ereg karegak di síbukaas sooluul. Jiliik kurimak kammi di 
karegak mati koo nuciikulaami di kurimak kan uliikenulaami 
• Say: Babaj ajaŋa ajuume alof di kabikak.  Waawu nalakoe ekaan to?  Jiliikaal karegak man 
jimanjaal. 
• Say: Jiŋar wan umanjumi di siciikaas di man jiliikooro karegak.  Nampi jilakomi eliikey di jiŋar 
musinkam mooluul man jiriiben furim fanoosani.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. They should whisper read (read 
quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If pupils finish reading early, 
they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have learnt to 
read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to remember their predictions from before they read the story. Give them a moment 
to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. Ask the 
pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
Pupils practice writing the letter
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "m" in a word in the decodable story. Call on 2 pupils at 
random to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "m"on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you do it. 
Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "m" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with the sound 
/m/.

activities.content:
Tongue twister-blend sounds 
• Say: Jiraafa jati Rama di Rohi.  Rama di Rohi 
baraane di jiraafaaj jooliil.
• Ask pupils what sound they hear most.
• Ask pupils what letter makes that sound.
• Say: "Ñaa ínje bee ereg uyel upinaay.  
Jinampenaal uyelaw tákon man jibajaal utingum 
kurim di ereg kalimoor." 
Say the sounds /m/ /a/. Ask pupils to blend the sounds together to make a syllable from the 
tongue twister. (Answer: ma).
• Repeat with the sounds /m/ /a/. (Answer: ma).
• Say each syllable "ma" "ma"
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them and say the word made by those 
syllables.
• Call on 1-2 pupils to say what word is made when they blend the sounds and syllables 
together.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud again
• Show the picture that goes with the story as you read aloud
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments. If 
pupils struggled with one of the new vocabulary words, pause to discuss its meaning in the 
story. If pupils are struggling with a new sound learnt this week, pause to point out the sound 
in a few different words.

Kasiitiilak di Ejaameney
Di funak fákon balaab man búbolie, ejaameney di kasiitiilak baraanab basofe so mámaak. 
Ejaameney di yommi, "Ujaal uñesaal mumelam man uraanaal."
Kasiitiilak di kumaŋumi di kommi, "Éey jaal man uñesaal." Di sijawumi, sijawumi, sijawumi
Di siteyumi, siteyumi, siteyumi.
Di múlamukaam di síriiŋumi di fumojaf (koloŋey).
Ejaameney di yommi, "Ñaa pan ubajaal mumelam man uraanaal!" 
Kasiitiilak di kumaŋumi, "Éey pan ubajaal mumelam man uraanaal."
Kasiitiilak di kubaalumi éloro di fumojaf (koloŋey). 
Ejaameney poop di ebaalumi éloro di fumojaf (koloŋey).
Kasiitiilak di kuraanumi mumelam - kuraan kuraan kuraan. 
Ejaameney poop di eraanumi mumelam - eraan, eraan, eraan. 
Di siraanumi mante soo búrom sipooñ.
Ñaa épuruley di ériiŋumi.
Kasiitiilak di kommi, "Fumojaf (Koloŋey) ésenkisenki, ínje let iŋoolen ípurul."
Ejaameney poop di emaŋumi, Éey, fumojaf (koloŋey) ésenkisenki. Ínje let i¿oolen ípurul! Buu 
nootaale ekaan?"
Kasiitiilak di kommi, ñaa ínje nimammanj buu nootaale ekaan eeno. Ínje pan imond iremboor di 
bálamukab booli man ípur. Nampi ípurumi, ínje pan iñakuli ípurenli."
Ñaa kasiitiilak di kaanumi moomu man kúpurulomi. Ejaameney di ewonkumi, "Jasiitiil, aw óomey" 
Bare kasiitiilak koo kumaamaal kábíñooney.
Di piyo jasinkun, jijaŋa yayinkun di jíjawulomi bee di fumojaf (koloŋey), di jijam ejaameen dihi elok 
di fumojaf (koloŋey). Jijaŋaaj di jirambenumi ejaameney man épurul di fumojaf (koloŋey). 
Ejaameeney di esalumi jijaŋaaj ban di emaŋ bee ejaw. Too galab, di ejukumi kasiitiilak di fulatenaf.  
Kasiitiilak di kommi, "Jajaameen, bonket úyolen kaneyaak di kumerak kúmboom kammojaat niŋoolen 
igoren fúkaaf fúmboom manoosani."
Ejaameney di elaaŋenoomi, "Éey, pan irambeni. Bare aw poop foo uliiken buruŋ bajoone ban oote 
karamben apaali."

activities.title: Comprehension – making connections
activities.content:
• Ask comprehension questions
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer the following question:
Question 1: Kasiitiilak buu kukaane apaalool ko? 
Answer: Jasiitiil bakaane apaalool kóje man akatuloomi dó di fumojaf (koloŋey.")
Question 2: Ejaameney buu ekaane apaali yo? 
[Answer: [Ejaameney bakaane apaali yo jak di esenool buruŋ bati karemboor man ápurul di 
koloŋey.]
• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss 
their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what is in the text or picture, as well 
as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have given them that idea.
• Make text-to-self connections

• Say: "Now, think about the way the Fox treated the Goat. What is the right way we should 
treat our friends? [Many good examples of help and kindness]"
• Ñaa jiwoonoor man kasiitiilak kukammi ejaameney eeno. Waawu eenomi wajakaaw wan 
• ceeŋumi man ukaan apaali? [Wajuupoe wariiboorumi di karambenak di kalegenoaak.]"
• Ask pupils to turn to a partner to share their answers.
• Call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss their answer with the 
class. Help the pupils think about how the story relates to their own lives and how they can 
use their own experiences to understand the story.

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the title 
"letters", "syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find 
the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who are not being assessed to read the 
story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: babaj kuñiil kalakoe fáreed, bare umanjutaal múreediwuma maanoe buu kookene.  
Jiliikaal karegak man jimanjaal.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Comprehension – Comprehension questions
activities.content:
Ask comprehension questions
• Thank pupils for staying on task and working well with their partners.
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer each of the following questions:
Question 1 Ayima aleebumi aba maalaay? 
• Read the sentence that shows this. [ANSWER: Please check from sentence 1]"
Question 2: Mata aleebumi aba maaalaay?  
• Point to the picture that shows it. [ANSWER: Please check from sentence 2]"
• After each response, congratulate, help, or correct the pupil's answer. If the pupil is partly 
correct or incorrect, tell them why. Help pupils find the sentence in the story that contains the 
answer.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the two flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Furimaf ufe waawu fufele ?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: "ínje bee ereg furim. Furimaf "Maama."Jíyentenoor jak man jileew butingum furim /
maa/ma/. 
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: "The word is "Maama." Now we have written the whole word. Let's read it together."
• Say: "Furimaf "Maama" Ñaa nuciikaaciik furimaf búrom . Jiliikaal síñakon. "Maama"  (Pupils 
read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the 
rest of the words.
• Words: minjen, Rama, kama, maala, mata 
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: "Now I want you to try and see if you can create your own words!"
• Say: "Ñaa nimammaŋ man jiliik man jijuk mante pan jiŋoolen jijoonenooro kurimak            
kooluul!"
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.
